title: Liberty and Prosperity -- Ch. 1: The 21st Chief Justice of the Philippines

one_paragraph_summary: Chapter 1 of 'Liberty and Prosperity' is the brief statement in which CJP accepted his appointment as the 21st Chief Justice of the Philippines, taking office, as he noted, in the 21st century. He said he accepted with deep humility and a great sense of responsibility, thanked President Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo for naming him to what he called the highest nonpolitical office in the land, and offered as his measure of thanks a vow to uphold at all times the constitutional ideals of competence, integrity, probity and independence, which he assumed she had weighed in choosing him. He read the timing of the appointment against the season celebrating the birth of the One who came down to earth to serve and not to be served and who embodies truth, justice and peace, and so saw the office as an opportunity for even greater service to God and country. He named his predecessor, Chief Justice Hilario G. Davide Jr., as his model, citing the aim in The Davide Watch of a judiciary that is independent, effective and efficient, and worthy of public trust and confidence, and Davide's parting confidence that the judiciary could do better still, which he pledged to fulfill. Reflecting on the heavy burden ahead, he took consolation in Pope Benedict XVI, the self-described simple, humble worker in God's vineyard, that the Lord knows how to work through imperfect instruments to bring about great things. He closed by pledging, with the support of his colleagues and of the approximately 2,000 judges and 26,000 court personnel nationwide, to safeguard the liberty of the people and nurture their prosperity while upholding the rule of law and the independence of the judiciary, in an atmosphere of transparency and accountability.
